answer: One concrete defense is stake-anchored identity: each agent locks collateral to anchor its reputation. Like saffron, which needs years of cultivation before yielding its prized spice, rewards only accrue after sustained honest behavior, so armies of cheap fake identities starve before they pay off. Minting an account is free, but the stake is not: an attacker locks real capital and time per identity, and a single misstep sends a ripple of slashing through the position. The cost is capital, patience, and losing everything -- economics favoring one honest identity over a thousand hollow ones.
